assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair to another without double-strand cleavage, a clear chemical principle (engineered deaminase tethered to a programmable nickase) that opened a genuinely new capability for precise genome modification. It is original, conceptually clean, easy to explain to a broad audience, and has generated a large therapeutic and research pipeline.
assessment.attribution: Liu is the clear intellectual leader. Komor (cytosine base editors) and Gaudelli (adenine base editors, which required directed evolution of a deaminase acting on DNA) carried out the decisive first experiments in his lab. Nishida and Kondo reported an independent deaminase-based approach, so credit is not entirely unambiguous, but the Liu-lab trio gives the most coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation is extensive, with many labs and base editors in use and clinical trials with human patients under way, so the principle is stable. Timing is good given the 2020 CRISPR chemistry prize; a committee may wish to see more clinical outcome data and may group it with prime editing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would rather recognise Liu for base and prime editing together, or treat them separately.
Weight to give the independent Nishida and Kondo work.
Whether recognition so soon after the CRISPR prize is seen as too close in subject matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation converts small molecules into inducers of ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, shifting drug discovery from occupancy-based inhibition to event-driven pharmacology. The concept (bifunctional PROTACs, then molecular glues) is original and generative, and it makes chemically new demands on ternary-complex design.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept; Ciulli delivered the VHL ligands and structural basis for ternary complexes that made PROTACs drug-like. Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a separable discovery that explains molecular glues and does not fit within three names easily. The split between concept, ligand chemistry and the cereblon mechanism is the central attribution problem.
assessment.maturity: Several degraders are in advanced clinical trials, and the mechanism is reproduced widely. No approved PROTAC drug yet, so the full therapeutic payoff is not established, which argues for caution on timing.
uncertainties: How to divide credit between PROTAC design and the cereblon/molecular-glue discovery.
Clinical validation is still incomplete.
Whether Sakamoto's early role should be reflected.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached high photovoltaic efficiency very rapidly, with long carrier diffusion lengths and tunable band gaps, an unusual physical property set for a solution-processed material. As a physicist I find the question of defect tolerance and approach to the Shockley-Queisser limit compelling, and the field has had very large impact.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park and collaborators the first solid-state, durable device, and Snaith the thin-film and meso-superstructured efforts that showed the strong efficiency and material physics. Kojima is not on the credited list, and Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have strong claims, so any three-person split will be contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and reproducibility are well confirmed, but operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up are still unresolved, so commercial maturity is incomplete. Chemistry recognition may be considered premature relative to the application outcome.
uncertainties: Contested credit, with Kojima absent from the credited names.
Long-term stability and commercial viability.
Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as physics/materials.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic-acid molecules electrically as they pass through a nanopore is a physically transparent idea that became a real instrument, delivering long reads, direct RNA and modification detection. It combines protein engineering, chemistry and single-molecule electrical measurement, which I find persuasive.
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived the idea, Kasianowicz showed polynucleotide translocation through alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered the pores, and Akeson demonstrated single-nucleotide-resolution reading with enzymatic control. The conception and engineering credit is spread across more than three people, and this is the main obstacle.
assessment.maturity: The technology is widely used and independently validated, with commercial devices in broad use. Impact is mature, though accuracy continues to improve.
uncertainties: I am unsure whether every credited person is living, which would constrain the final configuration.
The commercial platform development is outside the credited names.
Dispersed credit across conception, pore engineering and enzyme-controlled readout.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography uses X-ray free-electron laser pulses that outrun radiation damage ('diffraction before destruction') and enables room-temperature structures of microcrystals and time-resolved studies of molecular dynamics. The underlying physics is elegant and it opens access to previously uncrystallisable systems.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction concept with Neutze and colleagues, Chapman led the first demonstration with Fromme, Spence and others, and Schlichting contributed to later time-resolved work. Credit is naturally shared among more people than the prize allows, including some not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed at multiple XFEL facilities, but access to facilities is limited and the number of transformative biological results is still moderate relative to synchrotron crystallography.
uncertainties: Concept versus first experiment credit.
Dependence on a few large facilities limits breadth.
Real novelty of biological insight is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates formed by phase separation offer a physical principle for organising cellular matter without membranes, and bring polymer physics into cell biology. The concept has changed how many cellular compartments are viewed and is highly generative.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules behave as liquid droplets, and Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase separation. Pappu and Mittag provided physical-chemical framework and sequence grammar. The principle is broadly shared, so credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Interpretations are still debated, including the role of phase separation versus other assembly in vivo and how functionally important condensates are. Therefore maturity is limited, and I would see this as promising but possibly early.
uncertainties: Controversy over physiological relevance and over methods used in vitro.
Diffuse attribution.
Whether it counts as chemistry for a prize citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami folds a long scaffold strand with short staples into arbitrary nanoscale shapes, giving programmable molecular-scale construction with nanometre addressability. It provides a platform for nanodevices, molecular machines and single-molecule physics experiments.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund made the origami method itself, Winfree developed algorithmic self-assembly and, with Seeman's lineage of structural DNA nanotechnology, set the conceptual foundation. Yan advanced three-dimensional and complex origami structures. Seeman, the founder of the field, is deceased and not on the list, which complicates the citation.
assessment.maturity: The method is reproduced worldwide and widely applied. Real-world application in devices and therapeutics is still modest, so impact beyond tool-building is less clear.
uncertainties: Founder Nadrian Seeman is not credited and has died.
Applications are still emerging.
Which of origami, tile assembly and strand displacement is the core discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate designed non-canonical amino acids through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, giving chemical control over proteins in living systems. It is original, broadly enabling, and builds new chemistry into biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal pair approach in E. coli and yeast and Wang was the lead on the first experiments in his lab. Chin extended it to eukaryotic cells and multicellular organisms and to quadruplet codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama also have notable contributions.
assessment.maturity: Widely used, and the core method is validated in many labs. The impact is mainly as a research tool so far, with therapeutic uses just starting.
uncertainties: Several credible contributors beyond three.
Tool status versus transformative scientific discovery.
Therapeutic application is still limited.
